purpose: Discriminate the stock delayed configuration modulation without addressing or enrolling a valve.

calibration_setup_note.error: The serial calibration started after reboot with a zero runtime frequency correction. It therefore omitted the node-specific +122759 Hz pairing correction and landed about 47 kHz below the stock carrier.
calibration_setup_note.scope: Absolute center frequency from this capture is invalid as a protocol comparison. Deviation, transition shape, symbol rate, burst duration, and modulation-family comparisons remain valid. Candidate .8 independently established the calibrated live center.

wake_to_frame_boundary.conclusion: Neither stock nor candidate .8 changes carrier or deviation at the wake-to-frame boundary. All 304 configuration-frame symbols demodulate with the expected polarity.

interpretation: The stock delayed configuration is ordinary sharp-transition 2-FSK. Both GFSK variants have an approximately 14 us transition and are physically unlike the approximately 2 us stock transition.

The existing 0x45 deviation family remains the closest justified CC1101 profile. Register 0x44 undershoots stock while 0x45 overshoots it slightly; there is no configuration-specific profile switch at the frame boundary.
The broad modulation-family and wake-to-frame-profile hypotheses are falsified as sole explanations for the missing valve 81 50 response.

Code inspection found a different implementation-only discriminator: candidate .8 enters FSTXON immediately after the ordinary stage-1 reply and holds the synthesizer there for roughly 2.8 seconds before the delayed configuration. Stock contains no RF in this interval and is not known to pre-arm its synthesizer that early.

Candidate .9 must preserve every frozen byte, carrier, symbol, tail, and on-air boundary while keeping the CC1101 in receive configuration until 20 ms before the delayed configuration. It is not accepted until a valve-originated 81 50 advances the session beyond 2 of 6.
